The search results don't name a specific power station model, so I can't recommend a brand. They do show how to size one, and what size you need depends on your heater.

**What to look for**
- **Capacity (Wh) matters more than anything else.** [Off Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says a portable power station usually beats a plain UPS for reptile heat. You need sustained watts for hours, not just a quick handoff. Its pure-sine AC outlets can run the heat mat, clamp lamp, or thermostat strip you already own. Some units have UPS/pass-through modes, and transfer times vary by brand, so check the maker's page for the model you buy.
- **Runtime estimates.** [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage) assumes about 85% usable energy and 5–20 W of draw from the station itself. Its figures are arithmetic, and it says it found no measured reptile run on a power station.
  - A 24 W heat mat plus the station's draw is about 40 W. A 288 Wh unit lasts roughly 6–8 hours, and a 2,073.6 Wh unit about two days.
  - A 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat at half duty averages about 50 W plus the station's draw. That gives about a day from 2,073.6 Wh.
- **Rough rule.** Pick a station whose Wh is at least your heater's average watts, plus about 15 W, times the hours you want to cover, with some margin. Heat mats are far cheaper to back up than 100 W lamps.

**Before you buy**
- Dealectric notes most pet reptiles handle a short outage in a room in the 60s °F. It cites one vet's guidance of about a day for bearded dragons at 65 °F. Blankets over the enclosure, a shut room door, and hand warmers in an insulated container help. A battery matters most for longer outages and colder rooms.
- [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage) lists a home generator as one way to run your regular heating equipment. It also suggests hand warmers and wrapped warm water bottles as cheaper backups.
- Hatchlings, sick animals, and tropical species like chameleons are more vulnerable, according to [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pets-reptiles-during-a-power-outage). Size your backup for those first.

If you tell me your heater's wattage (mat or lamp), the species, and how many hours you want to cover, I can work out the Wh you need. Then you can compare specific stations against that number.
